mathgap.title: Signed Equality for Difference Statements
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates two differences, keep the order of subtraction on each side, treating both sides as signed equations (A−B = C−D).
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence says 'the number of X that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of X that C and D have' (or any similar equality of differences).
mathgap.example: Treating 'A has more than B' as |A−B| = … instead of preserving sign.

mathgap.title: Iterative Substitution and Propagation
mathgap.principle: Whenever a variable's value becomes known, substitute it into all pending equations and propagate the resulting values, repeating until no new values can be derived.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After any direct count, solved equation, or transfer that determines a person's count.
mathgap.example: Failing to substitute a newly known count into other equations, leaving them unsolved.

mathgap.title: Chronological Evaluation of Comparative Statements
mathgap.principle: Evaluate each comparative statement using the counts as they exist at that point in the narrative, after applying all earlier statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing a 'has K more/fewer than' or difference‑equality that appears after previous operations.
mathgap.example: Using a person's initial count for a comparison that occurs after a transfer that changed their count.

mathgap.title: Query‑Focused Subsystem Extraction
mathgap.principle: Identify the minimal set of variables and equations that are directly or indirectly connected to the queried person, ignoring unrelated statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Before solving, to reduce the problem size and avoid unnecessary work.
mathgap.example: Including equations about unrelated people, leading to wasted effort or confusion.

mathgap.title: Distinct Name Disambiguation
mathgap.principle: Treat each unique name as a separate variable, even if names differ by only a single character, and avoid conflating them.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Throughout parsing, whenever a name appears.
mathgap.example: Confusing 'Myles' with 'Myles' (typo) or merging 'Adolfo' and 'Adolf' incorrectly.

mathgap.title: Preserve Order in "Difference Between" Phrases
mathgap.principle: Interpret 'the difference between the number of X that A and B have' as A − B, preserving the order of the names.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When parsing sentences that mention 'difference between' with two names.
mathgap.example: Treating 'difference between A and B' as |A−B|, losing sign.

mathgap.title: General Comparative Interpretation (more/fewer)
mathgap.principle: Interpret 'A has K more (fewer) items than B' as A − B = K (or = ‑K for fewer), preserving sign.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a comparative statement with 'more' or 'fewer' appears.
mathgap.example: Swapping the sign, interpreting 'A has 5 more than B' as B − A = 5.

mathgap.title: Direct Count Handling with Overrides
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'X has N items', set X's count to N at that point, overriding any previous value for X.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a direct count appears, regardless of earlier statements.
mathgap.example: Ignoring a later 'X has N' and keeping an earlier derived value.

mathgap.title: Chronological Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: Apply each transfer (including 'gives', 'switch', and 'redistribute') in the order they appear, updating counts immediately.
mathgap.example: Applying a later transfer before an earlier one, leading to incorrect counts.

mathgap.title: Chronological Multiplicative Increase Application
mathgap.principle: When a statement says a person's count 'increases by p/q times', multiply the person's current count by the fraction p/q at that point in the narrative, after any earlier operations, and continue processing subsequent statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a phrase like 'X increases by a/b times' (or similar) appears among other operations.
mathgap.example: Applying the factor before later transfers that change X's count, resulting in a non‑integer answer.

mathgap.description: Swapped direction in 'has K more than' statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model confuses the order of subtraction in comparative statements.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always map 'more' to A − B = K and 'fewer' to A − B = ‑K.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes differences are non‑negative and drops sign information.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve the order of names when forming difference equations to keep the sign.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the chronological order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: Transfers are treated as independent constraints rather than sequential operations.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process transfers strictly in the order they appear, updating counts immediately.

mathgap.description: Treating 'has N' as an initial count regardless of position
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats direct counts as fixed initial conditions and never overrides them.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply direct counts as overrides at the point they appear, replacing any prior value.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats the increase as a final step, ignoring later statements that modify the same variable.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply the multiplicative increase exactly where it occurs, using the variable's current value after earlier statements, and continue processing any subsequent operations that may affect it.
